title: How to Recover Deleted Photos on Android
html:
Look in three places: the Trash in Google Photos, the Trash in your phone's Gallery app, and the Trash in Files by Google. Each keeps deleted items for 30 days. If a photo is in one of them, tap Restore. If it is not, and it was never backed up, there is no built-in way to get it back.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Menus vary by brand; the steps below are the ones the makers document.

I looked at these screens on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14, security update January 2025) on 10 Oct 2026. I only opened the screens and did not restore anything.

1. Google Photos Trash

  1. Open Google Photos.
  2. Tap Collections, then Trash.
  3. Touch and hold the photo or video you want back.
  4. Tap Restore at the bottom.

Google says items stay in Trash for 30 days and are then deleted for good. A restored photo goes back into its albums, your Google Photos library and your phone's gallery app. You cannot restore a photo that was already deleted from Trash, one that was deleted more than 30 days ago, or one from an account that has been inactive in Google Photos for 2 years or more.

Some older guides say 60 days for backed-up photos. Google's current help pages say 30, so use 30.

2. Your phone's Gallery app

Many Gallery apps have their own Trash. On a Samsung Galaxy: open Gallery, tap the menu icon (three horizontal lines), then Trash. Touch and hold the picture or video, then tap Restore at the bottom. Samsung says files deleted from Gallery are kept for 30 days.

Other brands (Xiaomi, Oppo, vivo, realme and others) have a similar "Recently deleted" or "Recycle bin" folder, but the name and the number of days differ. Check your own Gallery app.

On my vivo V23 Pro (Funtouch OS 14) the Albums app has a Recently deleted screen. It says: "Images and videos will be automatically and permanently deleted after the number of days shown (up to 30 days)." Each deleted item shows the days it has left; the one on my phone showed 26 days. In Google Photos, the Trash screen says: "Items will be permanently deleted after 30 days in the trash." I did not tap Restore on either, so I cannot say how it behaves.

3. Files by Google

Open Files by Google, tap Menu at the top left, then Trash. Find the files, tap Restore at the bottom, and confirm. Files stay in Trash for 30 days and are then deleted automatically.

If the photo is not in any Trash

  • Check whether a memory card is in the phone. Google notes that deleted photos and videos might stay on a removable memory card.
  • Check any other backup you use, such as another cloud app, a computer, or a photo someone else received on WhatsApp or email.
  • If you emptied the Trash, or the 30 days passed, and the photo was never backed up, it cannot be restored with the tools above. Be careful with apps that promise to recover it: we cannot verify those claims. Check what permissions an app asks for before you install it (see which apps can use your camera, mic and location).

To avoid the next loss, turn on backup in Google Photos, and keep it on. Google says your backup settings decide how and when your items are backed up.

What to do next

  1. Open the Trash in Google Photos, your Gallery app and Files by Google today. Do not wait for the 30 days.
  2. Tap Restore on the photos you want.
  3. Turn on backup so the next accident is not permanent.
